title: Disorder on the hyperbolic square lattice I: Anderson delocalization and absolutely continuous spectrum
abstract: We study the Anderson model on hyperbolic lattices. The graph is the Cartesian product of the Euclidean lattice with the regular hyperbolic square lattice having five squares at each vertex. We prove the existence of absolutely continuous spectrum and the absence of singular spectrum on a deterministic set of positive measure at weak disorder, and for $0<λ\le2$ when the single-site density is bounded below on $[-1,1]$. Truncated Cauchy distributions and controlled perturbations give purely absolutely continuous spectrum on intervals.
summary: This paper analyzes the Anderson model on a hyperbolic square lattice to determine if the electronic spectrum is localized or extended. The authors prove that under weak disorder, the spectrum exhibits a purely absolutely continuous component, confirming quantum delocalization. The methodology is highly technical, relying on advanced spectral theory applied to random operators on curved graphs.
main_problem: The paper investigates the nature of the spectrum (specifically, the existence of absolutely continuous spectrum) for the Anderson model on a hyperbolic lattice.
main_result: The authors prove that for weak disorder and under certain conditions, the spectrum is purely absolutely continuous on specific intervals, indicating delocalization.
method: The analysis employs advanced spectral theory, utilizing the resolvent operator, comparing path counts with coupling decay, and applying techniques related to Poincaré inequalities.
model_or_system: The system is the Anderson model, defined by the Hamiltonian $H_{\lambda, \omega} = A_d + V_\omega$, where $A_d$ is the adjacency operator on the hyperbolic square lattice $G_{4,5}$ (or its Cartesian product), and $V_\omega$ is a random potential.
key_observables: Local spectral measure $\mu_{\omega, x}$, the absolutely continuous part $(\mu_{\omega, x})_{ac}$, and the local spectral density $ rac{1}{\pi} 	ext{Im } G_{xx}(E + i0)$.
important_parameters: Disorder strength $\lambda$, the geometry of the lattice (hyperbolic), and the bounds on the disorder potential $ho$.
main_assumptions: The disorder potential $ho$ is assumed to be bounded and have a positive density on a central interval; the analysis relies on controlling interference between paths.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares spectral behavior (localization vs. a.c. spectrum) across different lattices ($\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z}^2$, hyperbolic); Figure 2 illustrates the hyperbolic graph structure.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the model and the goal (proving a.c. spectrum) to developing mathematical machinery involving resolvents and self-energies, culminating in the application of spectral inequalities to establish the final result.
why_interesting: The study of Anderson localization on non-Euclidean geometries like hyperbolic lattices is crucial for understanding wave propagation and transport in complex, curved media, which has implications for quantum chaos and disordered quantum systems.
